8868f7ca4dbb: Set Up MultiDatePick in Salesforce: Getting Started
d106769c7d2b: How to install and set up MultiDatePick for Salesforce
12513896dc58: Install the MultiDatePick package, assign a permission set, build a configuration in the Setup Wizard, then add the calendar to a Lightning page or a Screen Flow. No Apex required.
2e451f87c58b: Click Get It Now on the AppExchange listing and install for admins, all users or specific profiles. Then check Setup, Installed Packages.
1b87af94a637: Assign MultiDatePick - Setup to the admins who build configs and MultiDatePick - User to everyone who uses the calendars. MultiDatePick - All Access covers both.
e9f111f2f3a6: Build a config in the Setup Wizard
5e11d3775ced: Open the MultiDatePick Setup Wizard, choose where the calendar goes and what each pick saves, check the fields it fills in for you, and save. Or import a ready-made config from the Config Library.
385e8dea592c: Add the calendar to a Lightning page
6c80af3221cb: In Lightning App Builder, drag the MultiDatePick component onto a record page and set Config Name. On App and Home pages, answer the wizard's Whose records? question; only One record's also needs Static Parent Record Id.
b1299441dd4f: Or add it to a Screen Flow
407a4030c9fe: In Flow Builder, drag the MultiDatePick component onto a screen and set Config Name to your Setup Wizard config. Every checkbox setting comes from the config.
ff97dee00708: Do I need Apex or a developer to set up MultiDatePick?
1e49f24e83b2: No. You install the package, build a config in the Setup Wizard by picking objects and fields from dropdowns, and drop the component on a page or a Flow screen. No Apex required.
4441c79a3a0a: Which MultiDatePick permission set should I assign?
5937dfb6fbcc: MultiDatePick - Setup for the admins who build configs, MultiDatePick - User for everyone who only uses the calendars, MultiDatePick - All Access for admins who do both, and MultiDatePick - Guest for the guest user of a public Experience Cloud site. Users also need access to your own objects and fields.
0a497bf3663b: Why is there no Save button on my App Page or Home Page calendar?
e35e4821ed2b: App and Home pages have no record of their own. In the Setup Wizard, answer Whose records? (Just the person looking, Everyone's or Only ones that match need no parent; One record's asks for that record's Id under Link every pick to this record) and save the config again.
86b94154a973: Do I have to set every checkbox in Flow Builder?
2b7aa14b0ce7: No. Set Config Name to the config you saved in the Setup Wizard and every checkbox setting comes from the config. Only if you skip Config Name and set properties by hand do you set the checkboxes yourself.
0e8f2bf494e4: Can I move a MultiDatePick config to another Salesforce org?
c15d46a9ad23: Yes. Export it from the Existing Configurations tab, then paste the JSON into the Import / Export tab in the other org. The import lets you match any object or field names that differ.
025e2d7fd766: What Salesforce objects do I need for MultiDatePick?
8fcf7b484189: Book needs a booking object with a Date and a lookup to a resource object with a Name. Pick needs one child object with a Date and a lookup to the record it belongs to. Plan needs one object with a start date; a project lookup groups the tasks. Use your own objects, or the ready-made MDP Schedule and MDP Resource that come with MultiDatePick.
090a15ff445f: Which Salesforce orgs can use MultiDatePick?
38e5f6432000: Enterprise, Unlimited, Performance, Developer and Professional Edition, in Lightning Experience, including sandboxes and scratch orgs. On Professional Edition everything works except the guided tours and the Flow Parser action, which need Enterprise Edition or above; Experience Cloud guest booking works there too. Essentials and Starter are not supported, and neither is Salesforce Classic.

bebbdf6f46da: What you need: the objects for each feature
765cba84fe07: Book, Pick and Plan each save to Salesforce objects you choose. Here is the smallest shape that works, and the fields that turn on more. In bold: what each one needs.
ef19d9e2c188: Two objects you probably already have. Use your own, or the ready-made ones that come with MultiDatePick.
18b148712b60: <t1>Bold</t1> = needed. The rest turn on extra features: <t2>Start time</t2> and <t3>End time</t3> give time slots, so leave them out to book whole days.
0c943df12e52: Booking a person instead? A Task or Event’s Assigned To, or a custom object’s Owner, is the resource. No resource object needed.
92c4e790bfe6: No End time field? A <t1>Duration</t1> in minutes works with the Start time instead, and the calendar writes the minutes on every save, move and resize. <t2>Daily limit</t2> caps how many bookings a resource takes in one day, such as a technician’s two jobs.
1e2ee53cb2f8: Rooms kept as a picklist? Make them records: a room object with a name is what gets booked, drawn as a row and checked for clashes, and it holds each room’s hours and capacity. Salesforce allows no custom lookups on Event, so to book rooms, use a custom booking object (or the MDP Schedule) with a lookup to the room.
5ad124750ba5: Booking object with record types? The wizard’s <t1>Record Type</t1> setting gives new bookings one type or lets people choose, and the status list follows the type.
803143e3cb6a: Plan projects on a Gantt chart
f1b0d94bc21d: Tasks with a start, an end and an owner, under a project. Every extra field adds a feature.
9cf5f15bffb1: Hours a day or Total hours
89eb0171ab7a: Any record that groups the tasks: a Project, an Opportunity, an Account.
70aa97e968bf: <t1>Task link</t1><t2>only if a task waits on several</t2>
5eb42264a8f2: <t1>Bold</t1> = needed: a task with no <t2>End</t2> is one day long. <t3>Project</t3> gives one row per project, <t4>Person</t4> lets you turn on Workload (left blank, it uses the record’s owner), <t5>Waits on</t5> draws links and the critical path, and <t6>Planned</t6> dates give the baseline.

6e2f6d701c8f: <t1>Config Name</t1>. <t2>Static Parent Record Id</t2> only when the wizard's answer is One record's.
65e86e82913d: <t1>Leave every other property blank.</t1> The config supplies them. Anything you type in another App Builder property overrides the saved config on that page, so a property filled in by mistake changes the calendar without a warning.
dbfa1c961a93: <t1>On the page or behind a button.</t1> <t2>Show Inline (Always Visible)</t2> is ticked when you drag a calendar onto a page, so the calendar sits on the page. Untick it to show a button that opens the calendar in a pop-up instead.
eaca23fead24: <t1>New page? Activate it.</t1> After <t2>Save</t2>, click <t3>Activate</t3> when Lightning App Builder asks, and assign the page as the org default or to an app and profile. Until a new page is activated, no one sees it.

f44b14a14803: App and Home pages: whose records?
4f7153b565c0: These pages have no record of their own. The wizard asks whose records to show; <t1>Just the person looking</t1> is the default and needs nothing else. Pick <t2>One record's</t2> to save against one fixed record, and paste its Id under <t3>Link every pick to this record</t3>.
f15483301903: Copy the config name in the Setup Wizard, then paste it with the parent record Id.
b67f41d9f791: Full walkthrough and use cases: <t1>App, Home and Experience pages</t1>.
1de57b2b51ed: <t1>Bind Parent Record Id and every component saves its own records, no Loop needed.</t1> In Flow Builder, open a Screen, search <t2>MultiDatePick</t2>, drag the component on, set <t3>Config Name</t3>, and bind <t4>Parent Record Id</t4> to the record the flow runs for, such as <t5>{!recordId}</t5>.
442e2b55e8b6: <t1>A new Screen Flow has no recordId variable.</t1> Create it before you bind it: in the <t2>Toolbox</t2>, click <t3>New Resource</t3>, choose <t4>Variable</t4> as the resource type, type <t5>recordId</t5> as the API Name, choose <t6>Text</t6> as the data type, tick <t7>Available for input</t7>, and click <t8>Done</t8>. A quick action fills it with the record's Id, and so does a record page once you tick <t9>Pass record ID into this variable</t9> on its Flow component.
ace3c8358937: Drag the component onto the screen and point Config Name at your wizard config.
37746f667506: <t1>Checkboxes come from the config.</t1> Flow Builder shows a True and False choice beside each checkbox property. Leave them unset: with <t2>Config Name</t2> set, the config decides them. Only the flow-only ones (Required, Show Inline) take what you pick, and they stay off until you set them to True.
8acf6838d9c3: <t1>Who can run it.</t1> Everyone who runs the flow needs the <t2>Flow User</t2> checkbox on their user record, or the <t3>Run Flows</t3> user permission in a permission set. Without it, Salesforce shows “Insufficient Privileges” instead of the flow.
3a39f2934fce: Saves its own records. Read <t1>bookingSuccessCount</t1> and <t2>bookingConflictDates</t2>.

Add the <t4>Parse Date Entries from JSON</t4> action, loop its output, and create one record per entry. All clicks. Every detail is on the <t5>Flow Cheat Sheet</t5>.
